Eeeeeh. This article makes a lot of leaps of logic which are pretty much bollocks.

Assertion 1: Age of the carrier is over.

Not necessarily. While cruise missiles and long-range anti-ship missiles have removed the hegemony of carrier superiority in modern naval tactics, countertactics have developed at an equal pace. Anti-missile tech is at or one generation behind missile tech - enough to be effective - and given the changing nature of 4th-gen warfare the carrier provides a critical asset in global operations.

2: Russians have some needed experience

Emphasis on some. While the Russians did build a limited number of carriers, their experience in carrier operations and tactics is decades behind their NATO equivalents in the same way that their strategic submarine force was critically underexperienced - lack of funds and bureaucratic obstruction pretty much neutered their capability to experiment and train. Limited deployments, limited training exercises, and so on - saying the Russians know how to build carriers is like saying the French knew how to build tanks in WW2. Sure, they did, but compared to German tank technology it was primitive.

If the Chinese are building carriers for anything, they're building it for their growing influence in Africa - which is basically what the US is using their carrier groups for around the world. However, given China's less-than-outgoing foreign policy, actual deployments of any carriers they're using - outside of regional conflicts with the Phillippines, Japan, Vietnam, and Indonesia - would pretty much be for show.
